introduction-beyond-random-placement.core: By default the scheduler places Pods wherever they fit. Production needs control: keep workloads off special nodes (taints), attract them to suitable nodes (node affinity), co-locate or separate Pods relative to each other (Pod affinity/anti-affinity) and spread replicas evenly across zones and nodes (topology spread constraints).

first_principles.problem: All three replicas of a service land on the same node, and a single node failure takes it down.
truths: Related Pods may need proximity or distance.

analogy.title: Seating plans at a wedding
analogy.story: VIP tables, guests who must sit together, rivals kept apart and families spread across tables.
analogy.breaks: Wedding planners reshuffle easily; scheduled Pods stay put until rescheduled.

example.title: Problem and fix
flow: Add topology spread across zones and hosts

check.q: Which mechanism keeps general Pods off GPU nodes?
check.a: Taints on the GPU nodes (with tolerations only on GPU workloads).

taints-and-tolerations-the-bouncer.core: A taint (key=value:effect) on a node repels Pods that don't tolerate it. Effects: NoSchedule (don't place new Pods), PreferNoSchedule (avoid if possible) and NoExecute (also evict running Pods, optionally after tolerationSeconds). Tolerations allow but don't force placement, so combine with node affinity to dedicate nodes.

first_principles.problem: Expensive GPU nodes fill with ordinary web Pods, leaving ML jobs Pending.
truths: Tolerating isn't the same as attracting.
derivation: Add **node affinity** so they go there.

analogy.title: A members-only club bouncer
analogy.story: Without a membership card you're turned away, but having a card doesn't force you to go in.
analogy.breaks: Bouncers can be persuaded; taints are absolute for their effect.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Only ML Pods use GPU nodes.

code.text:
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-1 gpu=true:NoSchedule
# Pod spec:
# tolerations: [{key: gpu, operator: Equal, value: "true", effect: NoSchedule}]
# affinity.nodeAffinity requires node label accelerator=nvidia

check.q: What does the NoExecute taint effect do to running Pods?
check.a: Evicts Pods that don't tolerate it (after tolerationSeconds if specified).

node-affinity-the-magnet.core: Node affinity attracts Pods to nodes by labels using expressions (In, NotIn, Exists, Gt, Lt). requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution is a hard rule; preferredDuringScheduling... adds weighted preferences. It's a richer version of nodeSelector and works with well-known labels like topology.kubernetes.io/zone, kubernetes.io/arch and node.kubernetes.io/instance-type.

first_principles.problem: An ARM-incompatible image gets scheduled onto Graviton nodes and crashes.
truths: Some requirements are mandatory, others preferences.
Rules apply only at scheduling time.
derivation: Use **preferred** with weights for soft goals (spot, zone).

analogy.title: A magnet pulling iron filings to certain areas
analogy.story: Strong magnets are mandatory zones; weak ones just nudge.
analogy.breaks: Magnets keep pulling; affinity only applies when the Pod is scheduled.

code.text:
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      nodeSelectorTerms:
      - matchExpressions: [{key: kubernetes.io/arch, operator: In, values: [amd64]}]
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 50
      preference:
        matchExpressions: [{key: karpenter.sh/capacity-type, operator: In, values: [spot]}]

check.q: What does 'IgnoredDuringExecution' mean in node affinity?
check.a: If node labels change after scheduling, already-running Pods aren't evicted.

pod-affinity-and-anti-affinity-relative-.core: Pod affinity places Pods near Pods matching a label selector within a topology domain (same node, same zone), for example a cache next to its app for latency. Pod anti-affinity keeps them apart, such as replicas on different nodes. Required anti-affinity is expensive at scale and can leave Pods Pending; topology spread is often a better tool.

first_principles.problem: A latency-sensitive app and its cache land in different zones, adding cross-zone hops and cost.
truths: Inter-Pod rules are costly to compute.

analogy.title: Seating friends together and rivals apart
analogy.story: Friends at the same table, rivals at different tables.
analogy.breaks: Seating is done once; scheduler must evaluate rules against every existing Pod, which is costly.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Cache in api's zone, one cache per node.

code.text:
affinity:
  podAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 100
      podAffinityTerm:
        labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}
        topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
  podAntiAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 100
      podAffinityTerm:
        labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: cache}}
        topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname

check.q: What does topologyKey define in Pod affinity?
check.a: The domain (e.g. node or zone) within which Pods are considered co-located.

topology-spread-constraints-the-modern-h.core: Topology spread constraints distribute matching Pods evenly across domains (zones, nodes) with maxSkew (allowed imbalance), topologyKey, whenUnsatisfiable (DoNotSchedule or ScheduleAnyway), minDomains and nodeAffinityPolicy. They're the modern, efficient way to get high availability, better than anti-affinity for more replicas than domains.

first_principles.problem: Anti-affinity can't place 9 replicas across 3 zones and leaves Pods Pending.

analogy.title: Dealing cards evenly to players
analogy.story: No player gets more than one card more than any other.
analogy.breaks: Cards are dealt once; spread is only enforced at scheduling, so imbalance can creep in later.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: 9 replicas → 3 per zone, spread across hosts.

code.text:
topologySpreadConstraints:
- maxSkew: 1
  topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
  whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
  labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}
- maxSkew: 1
  topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
  whenUnsatisfiable: ScheduleAnyway
  labelSelector: {matchLabels: {app: api}}

points: Hard for zones, soft for hosts.

check.a: The number of matching Pods in any two domains may differ by at most one.
